summary: Zimbabwe sorts visitors into three lists: SADC neighbors and much of the Commonwealth Caribbean and Pacific enter visa-free, while most Western tourists — including US, UK, EU, Canadian and Australian passports — simply buy a visa on arrival from USD 30. A minority of nationalities must have an eVisa or embassy visa approved before travel.

notes: Australia's Smartraveller says photographing airports, military establishments, government offices, the President's residence and security forces is illegal, as is photographing demonstrations and protests.
Canada's travel advice says it is illegal for civilians to wear any clothing made from camouflage material.

payments.text: The UK government says Zimbabwe has a multi-currency system: Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) replaced the Zimbabwean dollar in April 2024, the US dollar remains legal tender and can be used for most transactions, and most suppliers prefer US dollars in cash. There is a shortage of physical US dollars, so withdrawals with an international card are not always possible, change is rarely available, and some businesses do not accept credit or debit cards.

safety.text: The UK government says there is a moderate level of crime: mugging, pickpocketing and bag-snatching are common in city centres, especially after dark, and there have been smash-and-grab robberies from vehicles. It says physical US dollar cash is short, power blackouts are frequent, demonstrations can turn violent and political gatherings should be avoided, and that you should stop at roadblocks and get a receipt for any fine.

tips.text: The UK government says the KAZA Univisa (USD 50) is valid for 30 days for travel between Zimbabwe and Zambia and for day trips into Botswana, and is sold at Harare, Bulawayo and Victoria Falls airports and at the Victoria Falls and Kazungula land borders.
The UK government says it is not always possible to withdraw cash with an international card and that change is rarely available, so it advises carrying small-denomination US dollar notes.

Zimbabwe's eVisa portal sorts nationalities into three categories: Category A needs no visa, Category B pays for and obtains a visa on entering Zimbabwe, and Category C must pay for and obtain a visa before travelling.

Australia's Smartraveller says photographing airports, military establishments, government offices, the President's residence, security forces or demonstrations is illegal, and Canada's travel advice says camouflage clothing is illegal for civilians.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Zimbabwe?
faq.answer: Category B nationalities, including holders of US, UK, EU, Canadian, Australian and Japanese passports, pay for and obtain a visa on arrival, from USD 30. Category A nationalities, including SADC neighbours, need no visa, while Category C nationalities must obtain a visa before travel via evisa.gov.zw or an embassy.

faq.question: How much is the Zimbabwe visa on arrival?
faq.answer: USD 30 for a single entry for most Category B nationalities. The official fee schedule lists USD 55 single and USD 70 double entry for British citizens and USD 60 for Chinese citizens (online visas), and USD 55 for a multiple-entry visa; it gives no other double-entry or nationality-specific rates. The UK government advises taking enough US dollars in small notes to pay for the visa.

faq.question: What is the KAZA UniVisa?
faq.answer: The UK government says the KAZA Univisa costs USD 50, is valid for 30 days for travel between Zimbabwe and Zambia and for day trips into Botswana, and is available at Harare, Bulawayo and Victoria Falls airports and at the Victoria Falls and Kazungula land borders. Zimbabwe's eVisa portal describes it as a visa for multiple countries in the Kavango Zambezi Transfrontier Conservation Area, valid for one month.

faq.question: What currency should I bring to Zimbabwe?
faq.answer: The UK government says Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) replaced the Zimbabwean dollar in April 2024, but the US dollar remains legal tender, can be used for most transactions and is what most suppliers prefer. It says change is rarely available, so carry small-denomination notes.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Zimbabwe?
faq.answer: The UK government says the visa on arrival is usually granted for 30 days and that to extend or renew a visa you go in person to the Government of Zimbabwe Immigration Department. No official source we could read states the length of an extension.
